theory.title: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados
theory.explanation: Usa get + participio en inglés informal para describir cambios o sucesos que le ocurren a alguien o algo: get injured (lesionarse), get better (mejorar), get stuck (quedarse atascado). La pasiva con get suele destacar un acontecimiento inesperado o un cambio.
theory.tip: Get + participio: get injured, get better, get stuck. Es frecuente en el inglés cotidiano.

patterns.label: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados · 1
patterns.pattern: He got injured during the match.
examples:
He got injured during the match.
→ Se lesionó durante el partido.

patterns.label: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados · 2
patterns.pattern: I got stuck in traffic on the way to the clinic.

→ Me quedé atrapado/a en el tráfico de camino a la clínica.

patterns.label: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados · 3
patterns.pattern: She got better after a few days of rest.

→ Ella mejoró después de unos días de descanso.

patterns.label: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados · 9
patterns.pattern: We got delayed because of heavy rain.

→ Sufrimos un retraso debido a la lluvia intensa.

patterns.label: Pasiva con get para cambios y sucesos inesperados · 10

examples:

→ El equipo antiguo se sustituye todos los años.

content.passage: During a charity run, one participant got injured and had to stop. A volunteer helped him and called the medical team. Another runner got stuck behind a group of walkers, but she soon caught up. After the event, the injured participant got moved to a nearby clinic. Fortunately, he got better after a few days of rest. The organisers promised that damaged equipment would get replaced before the next event.

items.prompt: Describe a time someone got injured during sport.
items.modelAnswer: I think looking after your health is about building realistic habits and making balanced choices. I try to stay active, drink enough water and get regular sleep. When I feel stressed, I take a break or go for a walk. It is important to follow medical advice and ask questions when something is unclear. Small changes can make a big difference over time, especially when people keep practising them.

content.audioTranscript: A: Have you got your appointment tomorrow? B: Yes, I want to talk about my daily routine. A: Are you doing enough exercise? B: I'm trying to. The doctor gave me some useful advice. A: What did they suggest? B: Drinking more water and getting enough sleep. A: Do you need any medicine? B: No, but I need to rest during my recovery. A: I hope you feel better by tomorrow.
